faqs.q: How many porta potties do I need?
faqs.a: For events, a common starting point is one unit for every 50 guests for around four hours, with more for longer events or when alcohol is served. For construction, OSHA requires at least one toilet for up to 20 workers and one seat and one urinal for every 40 workers above that. Call with your numbers and the count can be worked out exactly.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book?
faqs.a: For construction, a few days is usually enough. For events, book as soon as the date is set — spring and fall weekends fill first, and restroom trailers go before standard units.

faqs.q: What is included in servicing?
faqs.a: Pumping the tank, cleaning and sanitizing the unit, and restocking toilet paper and hand sanitizer. Long-term units are usually serviced weekly.

faqs.q: Where should the units go?
faqs.a: On level ground, somewhere a service truck can pull alongside, away from food service and out of the way of equipment. Avoid soft ground, steep slopes and spots where water collects after rain.

faqs.q: Do you deliver outside the city?
faqs.a: Yes — Broken Arrow, Owasso, Jenks, Bixby, Sand Springs and Sapulpa and rural sites beyond. Send a map pin for remote locations.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit?
faqs.a: Usually not on private property. Units placed on a street, sidewalk or public right-of-way, or at a public event, may need approval from the city or the event organizer. Check with them before delivery day.

sections.heading: Federal rules set the minimum.
sections.body: OSHA's sanitation standard for construction (29 CFR 1926.51) sets the floor. With 20 or fewer workers on site, one toilet is the minimum. With 20 to 199, it is one toilet seat and one urinal for every 40 workers. Over 200, one seat and one urinal for every 50. Those numbers assume regular servicing — a single unit shared by a busy crew fills faster than the weekly schedule allows, and that is when a second unit or an extra service visit is the cheaper answer.

sections.heading: What job sites around Tulsa look like.
sections.body: Oil and gas service yards, new subdivisions spreading south and east of the city, and farm and ranch work further out. Each has its own rhythm — a house build might need one unit for months, a commercial pour might need four for two weeks — so the order is built around the crew size and how long the job runs, not a package.

sections.heading: Where the unit goes decides how well it works.
sections.body: A unit should sit on level ground, away from where equipment swings and backs up, and somewhere a service truck can pull alongside it on service day. If the site changes as the job progresses — slab poured, fence up, driveway closed — tell us, and the unit moves with the work instead of getting boxed in.

sections.heading: Plan for the wind.
sections.body: Green Country storms move fast in spring, and wind is the thing that knocks portable units over. Units on open ground should be staked or tied off, and placed out of the path of runoff. If you have had a unit go over before, say so — the placement probably needs to change.

faqs.q: How often are construction units serviced?
faqs.a: Weekly is standard: the tank is pumped, the unit cleaned and the paper and sanitizer restocked. Larger crews, hot weather and long shifts can need more than that, and it is cheaper to add a service visit than to deal with an overflowing unit.

faqs.q: Do I need a hand-wash station too?
faqs.a: If there is no running water on site and the crew handles food, concrete or chemicals, a hand-wash station is worth having. Some units come with a built-in sink; a freestanding station serves several units at once.

faqs.q: Can the unit stay for the whole build?
faqs.a: Yes. Most construction rentals run month to month and stay until the job is finished. Call when the site is ready to clear and the unit is picked up on the next route.

sections.heading: Start with guests and hours.
sections.body: The industry rule of thumb is about one unit for every 50 guests for an event of around four hours. Longer events need more, and so do events where alcohol is served — people use restrooms more often. A 150-person wedding reception running five or six hours is usually three or four standard units, or one restroom trailer. Tell us the headcount, the start and finish times and whether the bar is open, and the count can be worked out properly.

sections.heading: Event season in Tulsa.
sections.body: Demand around Tulsa follows spring festival season, the fall fair calendar, graduation parties and the long run of outdoor weddings from April to October. Popular weekends book early. If your date is fixed, it is worth reserving as soon as the venue is confirmed.

sections.heading: Close enough to use, far enough to forget.
sections.body: Units should be close enough that guests can find them without a walk, but downwind and away from food service. Put them on level ground with a clear path, and with lighting nearby if the event runs after dark. Groups of two or three are easier to keep stocked than units spread around the site.

sections.heading: Standard, upgraded or trailer.
sections.body: Standard units suit festivals, sports and casual gatherings. Upgraded units with a sink and a mirror suit most backyard weddings. Restroom trailers — flushing toilets, running water and lighting — are the choice when the event is formal or the guest list is older. One accessible unit should be part of any event order that is open to the public.

faqs.q: When are units delivered and picked up?
faqs.a: Usually the day before or the morning of the event, and picked up the next business day. Tell us if the venue has access windows or noise rules, and delivery is scheduled around them.

faqs.q: Do I need an accessible unit?
faqs.a: For events open to the public, plan on at least one. The 2010 ADA Standards call for at least 5 percent of clustered portable units, and never fewer than one, to be accessible. For a private party it is still worth having one if any guests use a wheelchair or walker.

faqs.q: Can units be serviced during a multi-day event?
faqs.a: Yes. Festivals and events running two or more days are usually serviced overnight or early each morning so the units start every day clean and stocked.

pages.intro: Flushing toilets, running water, sinks, mirrors and lighting in a climate-controlled trailer — the restroom guests expect at a wedding or a formal event.

pages.seoDescription: Luxury restroom trailer rental for weddings, corporate events and parties in Tulsa and Broken Arrow, Owasso and Jenks. Flushing toilets, sinks and climate control.

sections.heading: A real bathroom on wheels.
sections.body: A restroom trailer has separate men's and women's sides with flushing toilets, sinks with running water, mirrors, lighting and heating or air conditioning. Guests walk up a short set of steps into something that looks and works like a bathroom indoors. For weddings, rehearsal dinners, corporate events and anything where the restroom is part of the guest experience, they are the right choice.

sections.heading: Power, level ground and a way in.
sections.body: Trailers need a level spot that a truck can back a trailer into, and a standard power source nearby — usually a dedicated outdoor outlet or a generator. Most have an onboard freshwater tank and a holding tank, so a water hookup is helpful but not always required. Check the gate width, tree limbs and turning room on the way in before you book.

sections.heading: Stations, not just one trailer.
sections.body: Trailers are sized by the number of stations — a toilet or urinal counts as one. A two-station trailer suits a small gathering; larger weddings and corporate events generally need a trailer with more stations, or a trailer plus standard units placed away from the main area for overflow.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book a restroom trailer?
faqs.a: As soon as your date is set. There are fewer trailers than standard units, and spring and fall weekends are the first to go.

faqs.q: Will someone stay with the trailer during the event?
faqs.a: Attendants are available for some events, which matters most for large or long receptions. Ask when you book.

faqs.q: Can a trailer go on grass?
faqs.a: Yes, if the ground is firm and level. After heavy rain, soft lawns can be a problem for the trailer and for the truck pulling it.

pages.seoTitle: ADA Portable Toilet Rental Tulsa OK | Handicap Porta Potty
pages.seoDescription: Wheelchair-accessible ADA portable restroom rental for events, parks and job sites in Tulsa, Broken Arrow, Owasso and Jenks.

sections.heading: Built to be used from a wheelchair.
sections.body: An accessible unit has a ground-level floor with no step, a wider door, enough interior space to turn a wheelchair, and grab bars beside the toilet. The toilet seat is set at a usable height and the door can be opened and locked from inside without strain.

sections.heading: Any public site, and most private ones.
sections.body: Under the 2010 ADA Standards, where portable units are clustered together, at least 5 percent of them — and never fewer than one — must be accessible. That covers festivals, fairs, parks, public events and most commercial sites. For private events the rule may not apply, but if anyone attending uses a wheelchair, walker or cane, it makes the difference between the event working for them or not.

sections.heading: Accessible means the route too.
sections.body: An accessible unit only works if someone can reach it. Place it on firm, level ground with a smooth path from the main area — not across loose gravel, a slope or wet grass — and keep the area in front of the door clear.

faqs.q: Do accessible units cost more than standard units?
faqs.a: They are larger and are usually priced a little higher. Call with your event details for a quote.

faqs.q: Can an accessible unit be the only unit?
faqs.a: Yes. Some small gatherings and job sites use one accessible unit, since anyone can use it.

sections.heading: A sink that goes anywhere.
sections.body: A portable hand-wash station is a freestanding unit with one or two basins, a foot pump for fresh water, soap and paper towels, and a gray-water tank underneath. No hookup is needed — it is filled and serviced with the units.

sections.heading: Food, animals and dirty hands.
sections.body: Food vendors at fairs and festivals are usually required to provide hand washing, and local health departments set the specifics — check with the event organizer or the health department for your permit. Petting zoos, farm events and job sites where crews handle concrete or chemicals are the other common uses.

sections.heading: One station for every few units.
sections.body: A single double-basin station placed beside a group of three or four units works for most events. Food areas need their own station, away from the restrooms.

faqs.q: How long does the water last?
faqs.a: It depends on how busy the station is. A busy event day can empty a station, so long events are serviced along with the units.

sections.heading: Sites without a restroom for months at a time.
sections.body: Oil and gas service yards, new subdivisions spreading south and east of the city, and farm and ranch work further out — plus parks, sports fields, farms and properties under renovation. Anywhere people work or gather for weeks or months without a building restroom is a long-term rental.

sections.heading: Set it once, adjust as the job changes.
sections.body: Most long-term units are serviced weekly. Remote sites with small crews can sometimes go longer between visits; busy sites and summer heat need more. The schedule is set at the start and changed if the crew grows or shrinks — you should not have to call every week.

sections.heading: Directions matter more than the address.
sections.body: For lease roads, pads, pastures and rural acreage, a map pin or written directions from the nearest highway is worth more than an address. Say what the road is like in wet weather and whether a gate needs to be opened, so the service truck gets there every time.

faqs.q: Is monthly cheaper than weekly?
faqs.a: Long-term rentals are normally billed every four weeks and work out cheaper per day than short event rentals. Call for a quote on your site.

faqs.q: Can a unit be moved during the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. As work moves around a site or from one site to the next, units can be relocated — just ask ahead of the next service visit.
